channel.title: LiVEUO — pharCare pharmacy software guides
channel.description: Daily guides on pharmacy billing, GST compliance, and inventory control for Indian pharmacies.

item.title: Two MRPs on one shelf: handling price revisions correctly
item.description: When a manufacturer revises MRP, existing stock keeps its printed price. Why batch-level MRP is the only correct model, and the counter conversation it creates.

item.title: Drug recalls: can you identify who received the batch?
item.description: A recall names a batch number. What it takes to find that batch in your stock, identify the customers who received it, and document the response — in hours rather than days.

item.title: Credit sales in a pharmacy: extending it, and getting it back
item.description: Doctor accounts, corporate tie-ups and neighbourhood credit are real business. How to set limits, age receivables, and collect without damaging relationships.

item.title: Connecting pharmacy billing to your accounting system
item.description: Posting summaries instead of every bill, mapping ledgers correctly, and keeping stock valuation in one place. How pharmacy billing should meet Tally or any accounting system.

item.title: Counter speed: pharmacy billing fast enough for Saturday
item.description: Where the seconds actually go in a pharmacy bill, and the changes — short codes, shortcuts, defaults, held bills — that recover them without cutting corners.

item.title: Cloud or on-premise pharmacy software: choosing your risk
item.description: The choice is not modern versus old-fashioned. It is which failure you would rather manage — your internet connection, or your own server, backups and updates.

item.title: Generic substitution: what software should not decide
item.description: Salt-based search, brand alternatives and price comparison help staff answer a common question fast. Where the line sits before it becomes a clinical decision.

item.title: Where pharmacy margin goes: five reports worth running
item.description: Gross margin percentage hides more than it reveals. The reports that show where margin actually leaks — discount, rate creep, mix shift, expiry and dead stock.

item.title: Hospital pharmacy vs retail pharmacy software: what actually differs
item.description: Indent-based dispensing, ward stock, patient billing and consumption accounting. Why retail pharmacy software rarely fits a hospital pharmacy without gaps.

item.title: Choosing pharmacy software: an evaluation checklist
item.description: Vendor demos are rehearsed. The scenarios to insist on, the questions that reveal architecture, and the reference checks worth making before you sign anything.

item.title: Training pharmacy staff on new billing software without losing a week
item.description: Most software rollouts fail at the counter, not in the data. A training approach built around the twenty actions staff actually perform, with a realistic first-week plan.

item.title: Refill reminders and repeat customers: retention for a retail pharmacy
item.description: Chronic patients are the most predictable revenue a pharmacy has, and the easiest to lose. How refill timing works, what to send, and where consent and privacy limits sit.

item.title: Pharmacy data: backups that work and DPDP obligations you already have
item.description: Patient data in a pharmacy is personal data under the DPDP Act 2023. What that means in practice, plus a backup regime that survives the failure it is meant to survive.

item.title: What happens to your pharmacy when the internet goes down?
item.description: Cloud pharmacy software is only as available as your connection. How offline billing should work, what must sync on reconnect, and what to ask a vendor first.

item.title: Supplier returns and credit notes: recovering expiry value
item.description: Distributor return windows, breakage claims, and the paperwork that decides whether a credit note actually arrives. Running pharmacy returns as a real process.

item.title: Purchase order automation: ordering from data, not memory
item.description: Reorder levels, movement-based suggestions, scheme evaluation and distributor comparison — replacing the habit that causes stockouts and expiry at the same time.

item.title: Barcode scanning at the pharmacy counter: what it fixes
item.description: Scanning speeds up billing, but its real value is batch capture and dispensing accuracy. Which codes carry expiry data, and how to handle packs with none.

item.title: GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for pharmacies: getting to a clean monthly filing
item.description: What your billing system must produce for a pharmacy GST return to reconcile first time: rate-wise splits, B2B separation, linked credit notes, HSN summaries.

item.title: Schedule X and narcotic registers: controlled-substance records
item.description: Duplicate prescriptions, locked storage, separate records and zero tolerance for variance. What controlled-substance record-keeping demands of your software.

item.title: A pharmacy stock audit that actually finds the variance
item.description: Full counts, cycle counts, and how to investigate a discrepancy instead of adjusting it away. A pharmacy stock audit procedure that finds the actual cause.

item.title: Why product-level stock tracking fails in a pharmacy
item.description: Two batches of one medicine can carry different MRPs, expiry dates and costs. Why batch is the correct unit of pharmacy stock, and what breaks without it.

item.title: Pharmacy billing software pricing in India: the real cost
item.description: Licence versus subscription, per-counter versus per-branch, and the costs quotes leave out. How to compare pharmacy software on total cost, not sticker price.

item.title: Multi-branch pharmacy billing: what to look for in software
item.description: Running three pharmacies is not running one pharmacy three times. What changes in stock visibility, transfers, pricing control, permissions and reporting.

item.title: Switching from Marg ERP to pharCare: a migration checklist
item.description: What to export, what to clean, what to reconcile, and how to run a parallel week — a step-by-step checklist for moving a pharmacy off Marg ERP safely.

item.title: How to reduce expired-stock write-offs in a retail pharmacy
item.description: Expired stock is pure margin loss and most of it is preventable. Batch discipline, near-expiry alerts, supplier return windows, and the buying that causes it.
